lines.W1.1: FanDuel, Flutter's U.S. brand and the #1 Sportsbook in America, is heading into the 2026 NFL season - which kicked off last night with the NFL’s first-ever regular season game in Australia between the 49ers and the Rams - with a package of updates designed to give customers more control over how they play. All three build on something that already worked elsewhere in the business: FanDuel Rewards Club builds from Casino's proven loyalty model for Sportsbook for the first time, Bet Protect+ moves from basketball to football, and AceAI gets a dedicated new entry point on player pages.
lines.W1.2: "Our customers look forward to football season, and this year we're giving them more control of their experience," said Karol Corcoran, Managing Director, Sports at FanDuel , adding that the goal is to make it the brand's most rewarding season yet.
lines.W1.3: FanDuel Rewards Club is new to Sportsbook, but not new to FanDuel: it extends a model that already worked on FanDuel Casino, rebuilt for how sports fans actually play. According to Aman Gupta, FanDuel's Sportsbook Growth Senior Vice President , it comes down to three things: transparency, choice and predictability, so customers know when rewards are coming, understand how they're earning them, and can pick the benefit that matters most to them.
lines.W1.4: FanDuel's boosts and bonuses have grown over the years, and along the way they've ended up spread across different parts of the app, easy to miss if you're not checking in daily. Rewards Club brings daily rewards, tier status and progress together in one place, with levels tied to each customer's existing level of play.
lines.W1.5: The choice-first design also ties into FanDuel's Play with a Plan initiative, which encourages customers to set a budget and think ahead about how they play. Gupta frames the launch as a starting point : "This is the start of the journey, not the end of the journey."
lines.W1.6: Bet Protect+, FanDuel's full-game injury protection feature, is coming to NFL wagers after a strong run through the NBA Playoffs and WNBA season. For a flat 3% of a wager, customers can add injury protection to a player prop bet: if the player leaves the game and doesn't return, straight bets are refunded in cash and parlay legs are removed and recalculated. It's a meaningful expansion of an idea FanDuel piloted earlier in 2026, when customer research found that more than half of surveyed bettors preferred paying for full-game coverage over accepting free but partial protection.
lines.W1.7: The NFL rollout adds two refinements: customers can now auto opt-in to Bet Protect+, including on bets funded with Bonus Bets, and the My Bets page will show affected bets in real time as injuries are confirmed, with cash settlement following immediately.
lines.W1.8: FanDuel is also overhauling its player pages with deeper game intelligence: full game logs, a rolling look at the last five games, and team-level stats including records and standings, with player prop trends, favoriting, injury reports and league rankings following later in the season. Sitting alongside all of it is a new "Ask AceAI" tab, bringing FanDuel's conversational AI assistant directly into the research flow. AceAI already lets customers ask about stats and available markets and add selections to their bet slip in one exchange. Since its wider rollout, FanDuel has pointed to a simple signal of traction: the more conversational the tool gets, the more customers come back to it.
lines.W1.10: None of these three updates started from scratch this NFL season. Sportsbook Rewards Club drew inspiration from FanDuel Casino's loyalty model. Bet Protect+ is moving from basketball to football. AceAI is getting a new front door on player pages. The pattern across Flutter's brands isn't single big-bang launches, it's taking what already works somewhere in the business and deliberately extending it: more customer choice in how value is earned, more control over risk, and faster ways to research a bet. The NFL season is kicking off. FanDuel is ready.

lines.W2.1: Sportsbet is using AI to expand the reach of its relationship managers, extending personalized service to more customers than ever before – while maintaining the personal touch crucial to loyalty.
lines.W2.2: Sportsbet , Flutter’s market-leading Australian brand, has tripled the number of customers its relationship managers (RMs) can handle, with no drop in satisfaction scores. This jump, from 400 to 1200, is no small feat in a business where personal service drives loyalty, and has been enabled by Jeeves, an artificial intelligence (AI) tool developed specifically for Sportsbet’s RM team. Like the fictional butler from whom it takes its name, Jeeves is designed to work invisibly in the background, keeping the RMs it supports operating seamlessly and efficiently.
lines.W2.3: “We know customers like having a dedicated relationship manager,” says Jenny Wishart, Head of Customer Platforms and Enablement at Sportsbet . “The question was, how can we make managing multiple customers feel like managing 300?” That's the scale Sportsbet is testing toward. As part of a pilot to see how far the model can stretch, one RM is now trialing a portfolio of multiple customers.
lines.W2.4: Jeeves runs on its own standalone data platform, separate from Salesforce, the customer-relationship management (CRM) system that handles Sportsbet's customer communications. The two are integrated, so Jeeves can read customer history and surface its recommendations directly inside the RM's existing Salesforce workflow. It can understand a customer’s personal preference and know when a situation calls for a direct conversation, rather than a more templated response, allowing RMs to focus on the skilled, judgment-led customer interactions that help build loyalty.
lines.W2.5: The highest volume of inbound messages to Sportsbet’s RMs relates to customer generosity requests – with 42% of customer inquiries about bonus bets and other offers. The speed and quality of the response directly affect customer satisfaction. But customer language is informal and varied in ways that are challenging for automation. Rather than “Can I have my weekly bonus bet?”, a customer might ask: “Have you got anything for me today?”
lines.W2.6: Jeeves learned to interpret these messages using 12 months of real customer conversations. Now, when an inbound message arrives, Jeeves analyses it in seconds. It determines intent, checks whether the message is a generosity request, and if so, makes a recommendation: approve, decline or offer a smaller bonus than requested. It then drafts three personalized responses with slightly different tones, for the RM to review before sending. If Jeeves cannot determine intent, the request passes straight to the RM.
lines.W2.7: A key measure of how Jeeves is performing is how often RMs agree with its recommendations. A year ago, the rate was around 30%. By April 2026, it had reached 69%, driven by both broader adoption of the tool and a recalibration in January that aligned Jeeves’s decisioning more closely with customer sensitivity and commercial metrics. Beyond drafting responses, Jeeves can automatically apply an approved bonus to the customer’s account, removing another manual step.
lines.W2.8: Bet settlement queries are the second-highest volume inbound category and the next use case in development. Jeeves is being trained on three specific scenarios: T&C explanations, bet deductions, and late bet cancellations – where a betting market remains open after an event has started, allowing bets to be placed on potentially known outcomes. In these cases, Sportsbet’s Risk team cancels all bets placed after the official start time, which can result in expected winnings being revoked. These are among the most admin-intensive interactions Sportsbet handles, often involving several internal teams, and Jeeves is being designed to deliver consistent responses across all three situations.
lines.W2.9: “If you were just a user, you’d think Salesforce was making all these decisions,” Wishart says . The whole experience is seamless: Jeeves appears as a window in Salesforce, reducing a process that once required multiple systems to a couple of clicks. But no recommendation goes to a customer without being seen by an RM – they accept, adjust or override with a different response if needed before anything is sent.
lines.W2.10: “The question was, how can we make managing multiple customers feel like managing 300?”
lines.W2.11: Designed with humans in the loop
lines.W2.12: Sportsbet’s approach to automation is deliberately cautious, not because the technology cannot go further, but because the company wants to protect human judgment. Jeeves leads on handling high-volume, routine decisions so RMs have more headspace and free time for nuanced engagements the algorithm cannot make.
lines.W2.13: Jeeves is deliberately designed to support responsible gaming by operating within strict scope limits and applying eligibility and safer-gambling checks, ensuring automated decisions are made only where it is appropriate and compliant to do so.
lines.W2.14: The current trial comes with clear guidelines: trust Jeeves for routine decisions, use its suggested messaging and intervene only when something looks wrong. Early signs are encouraging: the agreement rate, already at 69% in April, has climbed further still, to 72%. “It’s now about getting one person through that process so we can show the rest of the team that this works,” Wishart says .
lines.W2.15: The metric Sportsbet watches most closely is not whether customer satisfaction improves, but whether it holds. So far it has, even as customer portfolio sizes have tripled. If the 2,500-customer trial delivers the same result, it will further validate the model.
lines.W2.16: In parallel, a growing suite of outbound use cases are feeding RMs timely, insight-driven reasons to contact customers, complete with suggested language. “We can see if their activity has changed, or if there’s an insight we can act on,” says Wishart . “It gives the team a reason to check in and engage proactively with customers, with the right language and tone ready to go.”
lines.W2.17: Other Flutter brands are taking note. Sportsbet has shared a Jeeves overview with counterparts at FanDuel and UK & Ireland, with each brand charting its own path from there. FanDuel is pursuing its own use cases built on Salesforce Agentforce, while Sportsbet continues to expand Jeeves into new scenarios and is exploring how the platform could integrate with Agentforce to strengthen end-to-end capability, part of its ongoing work to scale AI-supported service without losing the human judgment at its core.
lines.W2.18: The original Jeeves made his master smarter and more capable without ever drawing attention to himself. Sportsbet’s version plays a similar role – ensuring that each RM can provide personalized service to vastly more customers thanks to the invisible magic of AI.

lines.W4.1: FanDuel has become the first official and exclusive sportsbook and prediction market partner of Real App , a social sports platform with more than 1.5m monthly active users that combines live sports data with community engagement.
lines.W4.2: Since the start of the 2026 NFL season, FanDuel odds, markets and data visualisations have been integrated into Real’s live game feeds, player performance screens and box scores. The partnership places betting-related context alongside the real-time statistics and conversations that fans are already engaging with throughout games.
lines.W4.3: At one level, this is a distribution partnership. More significantly, it reflects a broader shift in where sports fandom happens and how data, community and betting are increasingly converging around the fan experience.
lines.W4.4: For decades, the live broadcast sat at the center of the sports fan experience. Today, fandom increasingly extends across social platforms, creator content, group chats and live data experiences.
lines.W4.5: The numbers are striking. Recent research from Hub Entertainment found that 45% of sports fans under 35 get most or all of their non-live sports content from social media, more than four times the rate among fans aged 55 and older. Among sports fans aged 13 to 34 who use social media during live games, 62% say what they are doing relates directly to the game they are watching
lines.W4.6: Deloitte’s 2026 Digital Media Trends report points in the same direction. More than half of fans say social platforms are now their primary way of discovering new content, rising to 73% among Gen Z. For younger audiences, the second screen is no longer a distraction from the game. It is increasingly part of the experience itself.
lines.W4.7: The concept behind Real began with a 4 am text and a simple idea. It was February 2020, and Louis Antonelli messaged his younger brother, John, early in the morning, arguing the need for a platform that would turn real-time sports data into something fans could follow, discuss and react to together. They discussed a fragmented experience – one app for scores, another for highlights, another for conversation – where there was an opportunity to integrate.
lines.W4.8: Fast forward, and the Real platform now combines live statistics, play-by-play updates, player tracking, notifications and community discussion into a single experience. Every play, performance and box score can become something fans react to, debate and discuss together.
lines.W4.9: This approach has helped the platform build a highly engaged audience. Real says more than 70% of monthly users return on major game days, such as NFL Sundays, concurrent users have exceeded 250,000 during close games, and nearly 30% actively contribute comments and reactions. For FanDuel, this creates an opportunity to reach sports fans at moments when they are already deeply engaged with the action.
lines.W4.10: Perhaps the most interesting aspect of the partnership is that sports betting was already part of the conversation. According to Real's research, which has been published by FanDuel , around 75% of their users who commented on player performances had previously discussed sports betting. Users have also actively requested live odds and betting-related information within the platform. Rather than introducing an entirely new behavior, the partnership responds to one that already existed.
lines.W4.11: From a consumer perspective, that matters. Fans were already discussing bets and looking for betting context. The integration simply brings that information closer to the moments where those conversations are already happening.
lines.W4.12: The rise of platforms like Real highlights another broader trend in sports consumption – data is increasingly becoming content in its own right. Fans do not just consume sports through broadcasts. They follow player performance metrics, live statistics, highlights, commentary and social reactions alongside the action.
lines.W4.13: Research from WSC Sports found that 62% of sports fans have discovered a new team, player or league through short-form video content, underlining how sports discovery is increasingly happening beyond traditional channels. Odds can play a similar role. They provide another layer of context around what is happening during a game and can spark discussion, debate and interaction among fans following the action in real time.
lines.W4.14: 1. The fan journey is moving beyond the broadcast
lines.W4.15: Sports fandom increasingly happens across live data, social platforms and communities at the same time. With 45% of under-35 sports fans getting most or all of their non-live sports content from social media, being part of the fan experience increasingly means showing up beyond traditional channels.
lines.W4.16: 2. Data is becoming part of the entertainment
lines.W4.17: Fans no longer just watch games. They track players, follow live statistics, react to performances and debate what happens next. Real has built its experience around turning that data into something social. Betting markets and odds can add another layer of context to the same conversation.
lines.W4.18: 3. The best integrations follow existing fan behavior
lines.W4.19: Around 75% of Real users commenting on player performances had already discussed sports betting, while users were actively asking for odds and betting information. The partnership works because it responds to an existing behavior rather than trying to create a new one, bringing relevant betting context into the experience while retaining appropriate eligibility and responsible gaming safeguards.
lines.W4.20: The partnership reflects a broader trend across sports, media and technology. As fan journeys become more fragmented, companies are increasingly looking for ways to connect live content, engaged communities, and real-time information into a more seamless experience.
lines.W4.21: For FanDuel, the opportunity is compelling. Rather than asking fans to leave on platform and open another, this integration helps bring betting-related context into an environment they already use. This approach aligns with a wider shift in sports consumption, whereby according to Hub data, 41% of sports fans say they are getting more sports content through social media compared to a year ago. As sports fandom continues to evolve, the most successful experiences may be those that fit naturally into the ways fans already follow and engage with the games they love.
lines.W4.22: The significance of the partnership is not just reaching a new audience; it is participating in a broader evolution of sports fandom, one where the lines between media, data, community and betting are becoming increasingly blurred.

lines.P1.3: We’re shaping a world where life just works.
lines.P1.4: Through purposeful innovation and the strength of our connections, our technology keeps lives moving forward when it matters most.
lines.P1.5: Redefining What’s Possible in Claims & Repair
lines.P1.6: Millions of times a year, auto accidents and injuries occur. When life brings the unexpected, CCC gets to work, uniting an entire industry – insurers, repairers, automakers, and more - helping them come together to get people back on the road and back to health. Watch the video for CCC's vision on making life just work for the P&C insurance economy.
lines.P1.7: Every auto accident sets off a series of complex events that must be carefully orchestrated to get people back to their lives as quickly and seamlessly as possible. The CCC IX Cloud™ is the core of CCC’s technology. It integrates data and AI across our ecosystem to help insurers and repairers create workflows as dynamic and unique as the millions of claims and repairs they manage each year. lines.W3.1: From Surge to Stall: What's Really Driving the EV Market Reset - CCCIS
lines.W3.2: Explore what’s driving the EV market reset, including sales volatility, depreciation trends, and evolving repair and claims dynamics shaping the industry.
lines.W3.3: By Kyle Krumlauf – Senior Director, Industry Analytics
lines.W3.4: After several years of rapid growth and rising adoption, the U.S. electric vehicle (EV) market is entering a more nuanced phase defined less by acceleration alone and more by variability, shifting economics, and downstream impacts across the auto ecosystem.
lines.W3.5: While EVs continue to represent a relatively small share of the total vehicle population, their influence is expanding quickly in newer vehicle segments, claims activity, and repair dynamics. This report examines the latest trends shaping EV sales, vehicles in operation, claims outcomes, and repair economics – highlighting how the market is evolving and what it may signal for insurers, repairers, and consumers alike.
lines.W3.6: Sales and Vehicles in Operation
lines.W3.7: Leasing continues to play an outsized role in EV adoption. According to Experian, more than 58% of new EVs were leased in 2025, up from nearly 46% in 2024. Although EVs accounted for less than 8% of total new vehicle sales, they represented more than 22% of all new auto leases in 2025. This leasing concentration is expected to drive a significant increase in off-lease EV supply in the coming years: multiple units in 2026, rising to 600,000 in 2027 and approaching 795,000 in 2028.
lines.W3.8: From a vehicles-in-operation (VIO) perspective, EVs still represent a relatively small portion of the total car parc. Of the multiple million light-duty vehicles in operation as of Q4 2025 (Experian), about 5.7 million – or 1.9% – are fully electric. By comparison, there are multiple million hybrid vehicles (including plug-in hybrids), representing about 4.1% of VIO. Internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles continue to dominate, accounting for roughly 94% of vehicles in operation, or multiple million vehicles spanning decades of model years.
lines.W3.10: From an auto claims perspective, EVs now represent 3.7% of the claims mix, while hybrids account for 8.5% and combustion engine vehicles for 87.8%.
lines.W3.11: However, this distribution shifts significantly when focusing on newer vehicles. Among vehicles three years old or newer, EVs represent 9.7% of the mix and hybrids 18.5%. Over the same period, the share of combustion engine vehicles in this segment has declined sharply – from nearly 95% in 2020 to less than 72% – illustrating the rapid electrification of the newest portion of the vehicle fleet.
lines.W3.12: As the EV segment has grown, early attention centered on repairability and repair costs – particularly battery-related concerns. Increasingly, however, the focus is shifting toward the used EV market, vehicle values, and total loss dynamics.
lines.W3.13: Given the relative newness of EVs, the mix of potential EV total losses (valuations) is heavily skewed toward younger vehicles. In both 2024 and multiple vehicles aged one to three years represented over half of EV valuations. This stands in contrast to the broader market, where vehicles seven years or older account for more than 70% of all valuations, driven largely by older combustion engine vehicles.
lines.W3.14: In 2025, 12.7% of EV claims were flagged as total losses, representing an increase of nearly 2 percentage points from 2024. By comparison, the overall industry total loss rate was 23.1%. Combustion engine vehicles, which tend to skew older, experienced a 24.1% total loss rate (up 1.1 percentage points), while hybrid vehicles saw 15.1% of claims flagged as total losses (up 0.1 percentage points).
lines.W3.15: From a claims standpoint, this level of depreciation has several implications. It may contribute to an increased share of total losses within the EV segment, influence salvage values, and affect consumer outcomes – particularly where the gap between a vehicle’s value and outstanding loan balance widens. At the same time, declining values may make used EVs more attractive to cost-conscious consumers, particularly as off-lease supply increases, though concerns around battery life, degradation, range, and long-term value retention are likely to persist.
lines.W3.16: Repairable vehicle claims vary considerably by vehicle age when comparing fuel type. If you might recall from CCC’s Crash Course Q1 2025 report , hybrid and electric new vehicle sales took off in 2021. In other words, the EV segment is very young, especially when compared to the mix of internal combustion engine vehicles.
lines.W3.17: In 2025, more than 93% of repairable EV claims involved vehicles six years old or newer. For hybrids, vehicles six years or newer accounted for over 81% of repairable claims. In contrast, only just under 52% of repairable claims for combustion engine vehicles fell into this age range.
lines.W3.18: At the older end of the spectrum, 48.1% of repairable claims for combustion engine vehicles involved vehicles seven years or older. This compares to 18.6% for hybrids and just 6.7% for EVs, further underscoring the relative youth of the EV fleet.
lines.W3.19: Because of these differences, comparisons of repair costs often focus on vehicles three years old or newer to better align cohorts across fuel types.
lines.W3.20: This convergence reflects several overlapping factors:
lines.W3.21: The average TCOR for hybrid vehicles three years old or newer has increased by nearly 54% since 2020—outpacing other fuel types.
lines.W3.22: The increase in EV repair costs slowed in 2023 and 2024 and decreased slightly in 2025.
lines.W3.23: Hybrid vehicles have grown in size and incorporate increasingly complex mechanical systems.
lines.W3.24: Greater technician familiarity with EV platforms and improved parts availability have helped moderate repair cost growth.
lines.W4.1: Marketing in the Era of AI: How It's Changing What Shops Can & Should Do - CCCIS
lines.W4.2: In this space, we have talked about how shops can use AI as a practical, everyday tool. And while much of the conversation focuses on how AI speeds up estimating or improves repair planning, there’s an equally important shift happening behind the scenes: AI is transforming how body shops market themselves.
lines.W4.3: From customer acquisition and communication to digital reputation and operational efficiency, AI is redefining what effective marketing looks like for collision repairers — especially those competing in crowded local markets.
lines.W4.4: Here’s what AI really means for body shop marketing today.
lines.W4.5: AI Turns Responsiveness Into a Competitive Advantage
lines.W4.6: Ask any collision shop owner what causes them to lose the most leads, and you’ll hear the same thing: missed calls and slow replies . Customers aren’t willing to wait — especially when they’re stressed from an accident.
lines.W4.7: AI-powered chatbots and virtual assistants change this dynamic entirely. These tools can reply to website inquiries to provide answers about availability, services, or even repair estimates at any hour of the day. They can keep customers engaged even after business hours.
lines.W4.8: This level of responsiveness, once exclusive to large MSOs with call centers, is now available for ALL collision repairers, regardless of size. By appearing “always on”, businesses can capture leads that might otherwise slip away.
lines.W4.9: → Shops with CCC® Engage can activate the Carwise AI Assistant for use on their Carwise profile or download the plugin for use on their own website.
lines.W4.10: A Stronger, More Seamless Customer Experience
lines.W4.11: In collision repair, the customer experience is the marketing. Customers look to choose a repair shop based on trust, transparency, and the perception of professionalism — and AI amplifies all three.
lines.W4.12: AI-driven systems can really make a difference by personalizing interactions, providing real-time updates, and maintaining consistent communication through texts, emails, and chat channels. This means greater customer understanding, faster answers to their questions, and smooth, informed interactions, which can lead to an increase in overall satisfaction.
lines.W4.13: AI tools are even analyzing customer feedback, helping shops understand what drives satisfaction and where communication gaps exist. Shops that adopt AI-powered reputation management platforms like CCC® Amplify often see stronger retention and higher review scores because their communication is more coordinated and proactive.
lines.W4.14: Put simply: AI helps shops deliver a smoother experience, which turns into better word of mouth, higher star ratings, and more business.
lines.W4.15: AI Makes Damage Assessment a Marketing Tool, Too
lines.W4.16: Here’s a new development: damage assessment itself has become part of marketing.
lines.W4.17: AI-powered tools now allow customers to submit photos and receive a preliminary assessment in minutes — a capability that builds tremendous trust and keeps customers from shopping around.
lines.W4.18: What used to be a slow, manual process is now an on-demand digital touchpoint that improves conversion rates. Shops using AI to generate quick repair cost predictions stand out from competitors and create a modern, seamless first impression.
lines.W4.19: → Shops with CCC Engage can activate the repair cost prediction feature to give customers a range for what their repair may cost based on vehicle damage photos:
lines.W4.20: And when a customer arrives at the shop for a drop off, a more detailed AI-powered, preliminary, exterior estimate can be generated using Mobile Jumpstart in the CCC ONE Mobile App. More than one million estimates have been written using mobile jumpstart, generating approximately 84% of the final estimate amount in less than 80 seconds!
lines.W4.21: The Bottom Line: AI Is Redefining How Collision Shops Grow
lines.W4.22: For collision repairers, AI is more than a productivity tool — it’s a marketing multiplier. It helps shops look bigger, communicate smarter, work faster, and connect with customers more personally than ever before.
lines.W4.23: In a market where consumers expect convenience, clarity, and speed, AI gives collision shops the ability to meet (and exceed) those expectations — often outperforming even the largest competitors.

lines.W5.1: RT ProExec Launches Exclusive Community Association Program to Meet the Exposures Associations Face Today – Ryan Specialty
lines.W5.2: RT Specialty today announced the launch of its Community Association Program, a new liability solution for homeowners’ associations and more.
lines.W5.3: RT ProExec Launches Exclusive Community Association Program to Meet the Exposures Associations Face Today
lines.W5.4: The program brings pollution, technology, media and sexual misconduct coverage together with professional, management and general liability for associations and the managers who serve them.
lines.W5.5: Community associations have changed. Boards now run resident portals and online payments; communicate through newsletters, websites, and social media; oversee aging buildings and complex building systems; and employ staff and vendors with access to amenities and occupied units. Yet many of the coverage options available to associations were designed around traditional board liability and have not kept pace with these exposures. RT ProExec built the Community Association Program to address that evolving exposure.
lines.W5.6: “Association boards are no longer just managing properties and budgets. They’re navigating an increasingly complex risk environment spanning fiduciary responsibilities, environmental exposures, abuse, and more. Recognizing these evolving exposures, we developed this program to equip our retail trading partners with a specialized solution to better serve and protect their association clients,” said David Derigiotis, CEO of RT ProExec.
lines.W5.8: RT ProExec, an industry leader in professional and executive brokerage services, provides retail agents with deep product knowledge, innovative placement methodologies, and a high level of service to help them retain clients, win new prospects, and grow their professional and executive liability business. The Community Association Program draws on that experience, from the exposures RT ProExec brokers see in the field to the coverage needs their retail clients have asked them to solve.
lines.W5.9: Coverage for the Exposures Associations Face Today
lines.W5.10: Pollution: bodily injury, property damage, and cleanup costs arising from incidents such as sewage backups, fuel leaks, and fumes tied to the association’s maintenance and services
lines.W5.11: Technology and Data: Data & Network and Technology-Based Services Liability for resident portals, online payments, access-control systems, and website hosting, plus TCPA and FCRA coverage’
lines.W5.12: Media and Advertising: defamation, invasion of privacy, and copyright claims arising from newsletters, websites, notices, and social media
lines.W5.13: Sexual Misconduct: defense for board members and officers named in sexual misconduct allegations, including claims of negligent hiring or supervision
lines.W5.14: The Community Association Program is available now in all multiple states exclusively through RT ProExec. Retail agents interested in the program should contact their RT ProExec broker or visit rtspecialty.com .

The firm’s specialist brokers and underwriters handle an expansive mix of property, casualty, professional lines, transportation, personal lines and workers’ compensation insurance products, on both an open market and delegated authority basis. RT Specialty’s entrepreneurial spirit is combined with advanced risk modeling, market access, and claims advocacy to provide excellent solutions to its clients. Regardless of account size—big or small—RT Specialty is dedicated to providing lightning fast, expert advice, advocacy and execution on behalf of our retail broker clients. Learn more at rtspecialty.com .

businesses.reason: Current source lines describe an integrated claims business serving employers, insurance companies and government agencies. Components include claims administration, clinical case management, bill review, provider networks, pharmacy benefit management, ancillary care and liability claims investigation and resolution. Integrated services and CorVel's proprietary claims platform support consolidation; Marketwise Repricing extends the existing bill review workflow. Health and disability are named markets, but the evidence does not establish group health cost containment as a separately operated business or verify any completed exit. Source dates are unknown.

lines.W5.1: CorVel Launches Marketwise Repricing™ to Deliver Smarter, Market-Based Medical Cost Containment
lines.W5.2: CorVel launches Marketwise Repricing™, a market-based medical bill review solution that improves cost containment and pricing consistency.
lines.W5.3: A data-driven repricing solution that optimizes cost management and complements existing bill review workflows
lines.W5.4: As medical billing continues to vary widely across states, providers, and care settings, traditional network and re-pricing approaches do not always reflect market pricing. Marketwise Repricing addresses this by integrating market-based reimbursement methods within CorVel’s existing bill review workflow. This approach captures additional savings that traditional bill review methods may miss, ultimately reducing overall medical spend.
lines.W5.5: “Marketwise Repricing gives clients a smarter, more supportable way to manage medical costs when traditional cost containment measures fall short,” said CJ Cypcar, Vice President, Network Solutions & Product Integration at CorVel. “It strengthens existing strategies by layering in market-based intelligence, without adding administrative burden.”
lines.W5.6: Marketwise Repricing uses real-world reimbursement data and market-based methods. This delivers more consistent pricing that better reflects local market conditions. It also works with existing network strategies, making it especially useful for out-of-network bills and in states with limited or no fee schedules.
lines.W5.7: More consistent, supportable pricing outcomes across states and provider types
lines.W5.8: Enhanced cost containment layered onto existing bill review programs
lines.W5.9: An alternative methodology for complex or high-variance billing scenarios
lines.W5.10: Seamless workflow integration, with end-to-end management by CorVel
lines.W5.11: To learn more about CorVel Marketwise Repricing™ and CorVel’s bill review solutions, visit www.corvel.com .
lines.W5.12: CorVel Corp. applies technology, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and natural language processing, to enhance the management of episodes of care and related health care costs. We partner with employers, third-party administrators, insurance companies, and government agencies in managing workers’ compensation and health, auto, and liability services. Our diverse suite of solutions combines our integrated technologies with a human touch. CorVel’s customized services, delivered locally, are backed by a national team to support our partners and their customers and patients.

lines.W6.3: Return-to-Work Success with On-Site Job Analysis
lines.W6.4: In October 2021, a premier retailer partnered with CorVel to enhance the return-to-work outcomes of their workers’ compensation program. Offering local support and advanced technology, CorVel effectively provided on-site job analysis to help build the retailer’s job bank for modification-duty placement.
lines.W6.5: The retailer’s collaborative partnership with CorVel focused on optimizing employee well-being and operational efficiency for faster return to work. With on-site job analysis, an experienced CorVel case manager worked in tandem with adjusters and return-to-work coordinators to provide tailored solutions for each injured employee. The analysis served as the foundation for a comprehensive job description repository and enabled the provision of job modifications and light-duty alternatives until physicians cleared employees for regular duties. CorVel actively sought feedback from the retailer’s team during on-site analyses, fostering tailored program improvements and facilitating solutions to address safety concerns.
lines.W6.6: By leveraging CorVel’s on-site job analysis, the premier retailer realized cost efficiencies in workers’ compensation and promoted a safer and more informed return-to-work process.
lines.W6.7: "CorVel has assisted in revitalizing our return-to-work program by offering a dedicated team of return-to-work coordinators who proactively identify modified duty opportunities. These coordinators work closely with adjusters, providers, managers/supervisors, and employees to ensure legal compliance and timely return to work. Collaboration between the teams has resulted in a significant decrease in lost time from work due to injuries, leading to faster return to work, improved productivity, and lower medical costs."
lines.W6.8: Unlike conventional employer job descriptions, CorVel’s analysis provided in-depth insights into specific positions’ physical, cognitive, and emotional demands. CorVel’s detailed on-site job analysis enhanced the retailer’s job bank for modification-duty placement and fostered clear communication with employees regarding job physical requirements, thus streamlining the return-to-work process and enabling effective job placements.
lines.W6.9: CorVel provides vocational evaluation services to assess injured workers’ qualifications, including:
lines.W6.10: These services ensure compliance with statutory requirements and are designed to reduce workers’ compensation costs by preventing extended disability claims and retaining employees. CorVel’s on-site job analysis assesses job functions, physical demands, and educational requirements, serving as a foundation for temporary modified-duty and transitional employment programs.

businesses.reason: The current company descriptions affirm operations providing data, mobile, voice and managed services to residential, business, government, education and medical customers, primarily in Alaska. These related offerings form one integrated communications business supported by Alaska terrestrial networks, undersea fiber and a statewide wireless network. The completed name change to Liberty Capital Corporation preserves company continuity. Historical video expansion and the Dobson sale agreement do not establish a separate current business or a completed exit.

lines.P1.1: Liberty Capital Corporation
lines.P1.2: Liberty Capital Corporation consists of its wholly owned subsidiary GCI. GCI is Alaska’s largest communications provider, providing data, mobile, voice and managed services to consumer and business customers throughout Alaska, serving more than 200 communities.
lines.P1.3: Add to Calendar View IR Calendar
lines.P2.2: Liberty Capital consists of its wholly owned subsidiary GCI Holdings. GCI provides a full range of data, mobile, voice, and managed services to residential customers, businesses, governmental entities, and educational and medical institutions primarily in Alaska under the GCI brand. Due to the unique nature of the markets it serves, including harsh winter weather and remote geographies, its customers rely extensively on its systems to meet their communication, public safety and entertainment needs. Since its founding as a competitive long-distance provider, GCI Holdings has consistently expanded its product portfolio and facilities to become the leading integrated communication services provider in markets it serves. Its facilities include redundant and geographically diverse digital undersea fiber optic cable systems linking its Alaska terrestrial networks to the networks of other carriers in the lower 48 contiguous states and a statewide wireless network.
lines.P2.3: GCI incorporated in Alaska, founded by Bob Walp and Ron Duncan.
lines.P2.4: GCI constructs facilities and carries its first long distance call Thanksgiving Day.
lines.P2.5: GCI purchases capacity on the North Pacific Cable linking Alaska to the Lower 48 States.
lines.P2.6: GCI purchases cable television companies, allowing GCI to add Video to service suite.

lines.W1.3: Brian J. Wendling – Mr. Wendling serves as Chief Accounting Officer and Principal Financial Officer of Liberty Media Corporation, Liberty Capital Corporation and Liberty Broadband Corporation. Mr. Wendling has held various positions with these companies and their predecessors since 1999. Prior to joining these companies, he worked in the assurance practice of the accounting firm, KPMG.
lines.W1.4: Mr. Wendling serves on the board of Comscore, Inc. and has previously served on the boards of Fun Technologies Inc. and CommerceHub, Inc. He also previously served on the board of Clothes to Kids of Colorado. Mr. Wendling received his Bachelor of Science degree in accounting from Indiana University.
lines.W1.5: Philip J. Boeckman serves as Chief Legal Officer of Liberty Capital Corporation, Liberty Media Corporation and Liberty Live Holdings. Mr. Boeckman was a Partner at Cravath, Swaine & Moore LLP from 1999 to 2026. He joined the Firm’s New York office as an Associate in 1991 and relocated to its London office in 2000, where he served as Managing Partner and more recently as Co-Head of EMEA Capital Markets. Mr. Boeckman’s corporate practice at Cravath covered public and private companies and financial institutions, advising on a wide range of cross-border capital markets, financings, mergers, acquisitions, SEC reporting, governance and investigations.
lines.W1.6: Mr. Boeckman graduated cum laude from Westminster College in Missouri, where he serves on the Board of Trustees and as Senior Fellow for America’s National Churchill Museum, and received his J.D. magna cum laude from the University of Missouri in Columbia. Mr. Boeckman also serves on the Boards of the International Churchill Society and the Foundation for the United Nations Global Compact and was the Chair of the Society of English and American Lawyers.
lines.W1.7: Executive Vice President & Treasurer
lines.W1.8: Ben Oren – Mr. Oren serves as Executive Vice President and Treasurer of Liberty Media Corporation, Liberty Capital Corporation and Liberty Broadband Corporation. Mr. Oren spent the previous twenty years in various investment banking roles. Most recently, Mr. Oren was a Managing Director with Credit Suisse, where he advised companies across multiple sectors including Technology, Media and Telecom on a broad set of capital markets transactions. At Credit Suisse, Mr. Oren was a member of the Investment Banking Committee, Corporate Insights Advisory Counsel, Capital Markets Innovation Counsel, and Americas Head of Liability Management. Prior to Credit Suisse, Mr. Oren was an Executive Director at UBS Securities, LLC. Mr. Oren holds a BS in Economics from the Wharton School of Business at the University of Pennsylvania.
lines.W2.1: Board of Directors :: Liberty Capital Corporation (GLIBA)
lines.W2.2: Dr. John C. Malone is Chairman of the Board of Liberty Capital Corporation and Liberty Broadband Corporation. He serves as Chairman Emeritus of Liberty Media Corporation and Liberty Global plc. From 1996 to March 1999, when Tele-Communications, Inc. (TCI) merged with AT&T Corp., he was Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of TCI. Previous to that, from 1973 to 1996, Dr. Malone served as President and Chief Executive Officer of TCI. Additionally, Dr. Malone is Chair Emeritus of Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc., a director emeritus of Liberty Latin America Ltd., and Chairman Emeritus of the Board for Cable Television Laboratories, Inc.
lines.W2.3: Born in 1941 in Milford, Connecticut, Dr. Malone was a Phi Beta Kappa and merit scholar at Yale University where he obtained a Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering and Economics in 1963. He also received a Master of Science in Industrial Management from Johns Hopkins in 1964 and a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Operations Research from Johns Hopkins in 1967. He has received two Honorary Degrees for Doctorate of Human Letters; the first from Denver University in 1992 and the second from Johns Hopkins University in 2012.
lines.W2.4: Dr. Malone began his career in 1963 at Bell Telephone Laboratories/AT&T in economic planning and research and development. In 1968, he joined McKinsey & Company and in 1970 he became Group Vice President at General Instrument Corporation (GI). He was later named President of Jerrold Electronics, a GI subsidiary.
lines.W2.5: He served as Director of the National Cable Television Association (NCTA) from 1974 to 1977 and again from 1980 to 1993. During the 1977-1978 term, Dr. Malone was the NCTA's Treasurer.
lines.W2.6: In 1983, Dr. Malone received the NCTA Vanguard Award, one of the highest honors in the cable television industry. He has received many other awards and honors which include: TVC Magazine Man of the Year Award - 1981; Wall Street Transcript's Gold Award for the cable industry's best Chief Executive Officer - 1982, 1985, 1986 and 1987; Wall Street Transcript’s Silver Award in 1984 and 1989; Women In Cable's Betsy Magness Fellowship Honoree; University of Pennsylvania Wharton School Sol C. Snider Entrepreneurial Center Award of Merit for Distinguished Entrepreneurship; American Jewish Committee Sherrill C. Corwin Human Relations Award; Communications Technology Magazine Service and Technology Award; Bronze Award - 1993 Financial World CEO of the Year Competition; The Hopkins Distinguished Alumnus Award in 1994 and in 2004 the Hopkins Medal, the school’s highest award. He is also recognized as a Yale Sterling Fellow (Harkness Circle) and in May of 2016 he was awarded the Steven J. Ross Humanitarian Award. In October of 2016, Dr. Malone was honored by the Television Academy with the Charles F. Jenkins Lifetime Achievement Emmy Award. On January 9, 2017 he received the Citizen of the West award which is an honor bestowed upon him through the National Western Association in Colorado.
lines.W2.7: Brian M. Deevy – Mr. Deevy has served a director of Liberty Media Corporation since June 2015, as a director of Atlanta Braves Holdings, Inc since 2023, and as a director of Liberty Capital since July 2025. He previously served as the head of Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) Capital Markets’ Communications, Media & Entertainment (CME) Group. Mr. Deevy was responsible for strategic development of the CME Group’s business, which included mergers & acquisitions, private equity and debt capital formation, and financial advisory engagements. He also served as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Daniels & Associates, the investment banking firm that provided financial advisory services to the communications industry until it was acquired by RBC in 2007. Prior to joining Daniels & Associates, RBC Daniels’ predecessor, Mr. Deevy was with Continental Illinois National Bank. Mr. Deevy has served as a director of the Daniels Fund since 2003, and a Director of the U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Foundation from 2016 to 2024.
lines.W2.8: Mr. Deevy earned a bachelor's degree from Dartmouth College and an MBA from the Amos Tuck School of Business Administration at Dartmouth.
lines.W2.9: Mr. Gould is a co-founder of Mediabids.com, Inc. (“Mediabids”) and has served as its President and CEO since its founding in 1999. Mediabids operates an extensive print advertising network across the U.S., specializing in response-based solutions in newspaper and magazine advertising. Since 2021, Mr. Gould has also served as a director of The Baltimore Banner and Venetoulis Institute for Local Journalism, a non-profit organization committed to bringing high-quality local journalism to Baltimore and central Maryland through its operation of The Baltimore Banner. Since 2024, Mr. Gould has served as President of the board of directors of KRBD Public Radio, a community radio station for southern southeast Alaska.
lines.W2.10: Dr. Richard Green – Mr. Green has served as a director of Liberty Broadband since November 2014, and as a director of Liberty Capital since July 2025. Green has served as a director of Liberty Global plc and its predecessors since December 2008. He has also served as a director of Shaw Communications, Inc., a telecommunications company based in Canada, since 2010. Green serves as a director of Jones/NCTI, a Jones Knowledge Company, which is a workforce performance solutions company for individuals and broadband companies. He is former Chairman of the Space Science Institute in Boulder, Colorado. He is a Professor of Engineering and Director of the Center of Technology and Innovation at University of Denver.
lines.W2.11: Green is the former President and CEO of CableLabs®. Before joining CableLabs®, Green served as an executive for three television networks, ABC, CBS, and PBS. In 2012, Green received an Emmy for Lifetime Achievement from the Academy of Television Arts & Sciences for technical contributions to television. He is also a member of the Cable Television Hall of Fame.
lines.W2.12: Larry E. Romrell – Mr. Romrell has served as a director of Liberty Media since May 2006 and was a director of Old Liberty from March 1999 to May 2006. Romrell has served as a director of Liberty Capital since July 2025. He is also a director of LGI. Mr. Romrell served as an Executive Vice President of TCI from January 1994 to March 1999.

lines.P1.1: Concrete Pumping Holdings, Inc.
lines.P1.2: Concrete Pumping Holdings is the leading provider of concrete pumping services and concrete waste management solutions in the U.S. and U.K., operating under the only established, national brands in both countries.
lines.P1.3: Concrete Pumping Holdings is the leading provider of concrete pumping services in the highly fragmented U.S. and U.K. markets, operating under the only established, national brands in both markets (Brundage-Bone and Camfaud, respectively). Concrete pumping is a "mission-critical" method of concrete placement that requires highly-skilled operators to position a truck-mounted fully-articulating boom for precise delivery of ready-mix concrete from mixer trucks to placing crews on a job site. CPH's large fleet of specialized pumping equipment and highly-trained operators position CPH to deliver concrete placement solutions that facilitate substantial labor cost savings to customers, shorten concrete placement times, enhance worksite safety and improve construction quality. CPH operates a fee-based revenue model with no bonding requirements.
lines.P1.4: CPH is also the leading provider of concrete waste management services in the U.S. market, operating under the only established, national brand, Eco-Pan. Highly complementary to its core concrete pumping service, Eco-Pan provides a full-service, cost-effective, regulatory-compliant solution to manage environmental issues caused by concrete washout.
lines.P1.5: As of, the Company provided concrete pumping services in the U.S. from a footprint of multiple branch locations across approximately 20 states, concrete pumping services in the U.K. from multiple branch locations, and route-based concrete waste management services from multiple operating locations in the U.S. and 1 shared location in the U.K.

lines.P3.2: Brundage-Bone is the largest concrete pumping and material placement service in the United States. with just one location in Denver, Colorado, Brundage-Bone provides concrete pumping services in the U.S. with a fleet of 482 equipment units from a highly diversified footprint of multiple locations across 22 states (as of). Since our origin we have more experience pumping concrete than anyone. Brundage-Bone supplies the largest and most diverse fleet of concrete pumping vehicles and equipment with the most multi-regional locations across the nation. Due to our vast knowledge of concrete pumping, we continue to lead the industry in technology, customer service, fleet and location size, training, and safety.

lines.W2.1: Concrete Waste Management Services - Eco-Pan :: Concrete Pumping Holdings, Inc. (BBCP)
lines.W2.2: Eco-Pan is the leader in concrete waste management services. We help our customers comply with environmental regulations, avoid fines, and recue their compliance costs. We deliver watertight pans to job sites to collect concrete washwater and pick up the pans to deliver to recycling centers for a turn-key solution to customers compared to the alternatives. Our commitment to customer service, the time-saving methods of handling concrete waste disposal for our customers and the prompt service in getting the washout bins you need is second-to-none. Eco-Pan is a unique industrial washout containment system designed to contain cementitious materials from industrial and construction sites, which may be harmful to the environment. Our unique design allows for site portability and ease of handling, and our response times help contractors comply with today's job site BMP's, SWPPP requirements and LEED recycling. As of April 30, 2018, Eco-Pan operates out of twelve markets in the United States, but is expanding to meet customer needs.

lines.W3.17: EBITDA is calculated by taking GAAP net income and adding back interest expense and amortization of deferred financing costs net of interest income, income tax expense, and depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA is calculated by taking EBITDA and adding back transaction expenses, loss on debt extinguishment, stock-based compensation, other expense (income), net, goodwill and intangibles impairment and other adjustments. Other adjustments include non-recurring expenses, non-cash currency gains/losses and research and development expenses. Transaction expenses represent expenses for legal, accounting, and other professionals that were engaged in the completion of various acquisitions. Transaction expenses can be volatile as they are primarily driven by the size of a specific acquisition. As such, the Company excludes these amounts from Adjusted EBITDA for comparability across periods.
lines.W3.18: Net debt as a specified date is calculated as all amounts outstanding under debt agreements (currently this includes the Company’s term loan and revolving line of credit balances, excluding any offsets for capitalized deferred financing costs) measured in accordance with GAAP less cash. Cash is subtracted from the GAAP measure because it could be used to reduce the Company’s debt obligations. A limitation associated with using net debt is that it subtracts cash and therefore may imply that there is less Company debt than the most comparable GAAP measure indicates. CPH believes this non-GAAP measure provides useful information to management and investors in order to monitor the Company’s leverage and evaluate the Company’s consolidated balance sheet. See "Reconciliation of Net Debt" below for a reconciliation of Net Debt to amounts outstanding under debt agreements calculated in accordance with GAAP.
lines.W3.19: The leverage ratio is defined as the ratio of net debt to Adjusted EBITDA for the trailing four quarters. The Company believes its leverage ratio measures its ability to service its debt and its ability to make capital expenditures. Additionally, the leverage ratio is a standard measurement used by investors to gauge the creditworthiness of an institution.

Partner offerings extend the same customized products and stuffing experience to companies and organizations through wholesale, bulk orders, and events; the evidence does not establish a separate economic business. The sources are undated, limiting verification of recency as of 2026-10-27. Franchise royalties, repair services, and separate party fees from the prior hypothesis are not verified by the cited lines.

lines.W2.1: Build-A-Bear | Shipping & Delivery Information
lines.W2.2: Where’s My Order | Order Summary | Tracking | Shipping Information
lines.W2.3: Your order goes though the following steps once it has been placed. You will receive 3 emails: Order Confirmation, Order is Being Prepared, and Shipment Confirmation.
lines.W2.4: Enter your order information to view a summary which includes items orders, order status, and a tracking number. Please note that the tracking number is available once the order has left our warehouse. A shipment confirmation email with a tracking number will also be sent.
lines.W2.5: Once your order has left our warehouse you will receive a shipment confirmation email with a tracking number. If you have your tracking number from the shipment confirmation email, you can enter it here to track your order.
lines.W2.6: If you have your Order ID number from either Global-e or Build-A-Bear, you can enter it here to track your order.
lines.W2.7: Do You Offer Expedited Shipping Methods?
lines.W2.8: We currently offer FedEx Express Shipping and Same-Day Delivery by Uber. Buy Online, Pick Up in Store is also a convenient option for getting your items fast.
lines.W2.9: How Long Does it Take to Receive My Order, and How Much Will it Cost to Ship?
lines.W2.10: Shipping times depend on the type of service requested. Please see the table below for regular shipping costs.
lines.W2.11: Same Day* Delivery by Uber
lines.W2.12: *Same-Day Delivery eligibility is dependent on Workshop availability within 20 driving miles of your delivery address. Product availability may vary by location, and not all items shown online are available in stores (including but not limited to online exclusive items and embroidered plush). Orders must be placed by 12 p.m. local time for Same-Day Delivery; orders placed after 12 p.m. may be delivered the next day. Your Uber Delivery Driver may text you to let you know when your order has been delivered or if they have any questions.
lines.W2.13: A separate order must be placed for each shipping address.
lines.W2.14: FedEx shipping is not available for International orders.
lines.W2.15: FedEx Next Day Service and FedEx 2 Day Service are not available for P.O. boxes, rural routes, and FPO/APO addresses.
lines.W2.16: FedEx Standard Delivery is not available for shipments to Puerto Rico and other US territories, P.O. boxes, and FPO/APO addresses.
lines.W2.17: International deliveries may be made to most locations outside of the United States. Unfortunately, we cannot ship to Mexico, Costa Rica, Israel, Kenya, Malaysia, Pakistan, Thailand, Ukraine, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Russia, Uganda, and Nigeria at this time due to complex customs regulations and high-dollar duty charges.
lines.W2.18: Orders are shipped via Parcel Post/Air Mail and take 6-21 business days to reach their destination. Shipping fees do not include duties, custom charges, or value-added taxes. Please include the postal code in the international address so your order may be processed on time. Orders that include a personalized Record Your Voice message require additional processing days to fulfill.
lines.W2.19: Orders shipped to Canada are shipped through Global-E, and do include duties, taxes, and conversions
lines.W2.20: Our prices do not include duties, value-added taxes (VAT) or miscellaneous fees. If assessed, these charges are the responsibility of the package recipient, who will be billed for them by the local Customs office. Please keep this in mind when shipping a gift item to a destination outside the U.S. You may be contacted by your local carrier prior to delivery, to settle any outstanding duties, taxes or fees.
lines.W2.21: Can I Ship a Package to an APO / FPO Address?
lines.W2.22: Yes, we do ship to military bases. Please enter the APO/FPO unit as the address; enter APO or FPO as the city; and for the state, please select one of the following:
lines.W2.23: Select United States for the country, and enter the correct Zip Code for the APO/FPO destination. You will not be charged tax for an APO/FPO address, and all orders must be shipped as FedEx Economy.
lines.W2.24: Why Don't I See My Country on the List of Countries When Trying to Place My Order?
lines.W2.25: Due to current licensing agreements, select furry friends and clothes are only available in certain countries. These limitations apply to both shipping and billing addresses. You will not be able to select your country in checkout if the furry friends in your cart are restricted in your area.
lines.W3.1: The Office Stuffed Animals | Build-A-Bear
lines.W3.2: Shop The Office Stuffed Animals at Build-A-Bear Workshop®. Personalize with clothing, accessories & more online or in our Workshops.
lines.W3.3: Bring the hilarious, dysfunctional world of Dunder Mifflin to life with Build-A-Bear's The Office plush toy collection!
lines.W3.4: Featuring plush toys, clothing, and accessories inspired by the hit comedy series, this collection is perfect for fans of Dunder Mifflin. Whether you're recreating classic moments, showing off your favorite character’s signature style, or just looking for a fun way to celebrate your love for the show, these cuddly companions bring the laughs to any collection. Dress your plush in themed outfits and accessories at a store near you or through our online Bear Builder to capture the charm and humor of Scranton’s finest.
lines.W3.5: Make your The Office plush even more fun with a custom voice message ! Add a favorite quote, an iconic theme song snippet, or a personal message to make your plush one-of-a-kind. Simply record a 5 to 30-second clip at home or in store and our Bear Builders can add your special message to any stuffed animal. With hilarious clothing, memorable accessories, and personalized sound options, Build-A-Bear’s The Office collection is the perfect way to bring a little workplace comedy to your plush lineup.
